$comment: Per-human deployment records driven by elohim/holochain/Jenkinsfile. All humans now run the consolidated single-container pattern (elohim-node) — see genesis/orchestrator/manifests/humans/_edgenode-consolidated.template.yaml for the shared template. Adam uses an explicit manifest file (the historical reference impl); everyone else sed-renders the template. See genesis/plans/2026-04-16-elohim-node-consolidation-design.md for background and 2026-04-21-consolidate-human-deployments.md for the migration that retired the legacy 4-container pattern. The edgenode{Memory,Cpu}{Request,Limit} fields are THE source of truth for per-human conductor resource budgets — each set is tied to a deviceArchetype from genesis/plans/2026-04-13-device-archetypes-design.md. Treat these as the archetype's validated minimum; when bumped temporarily to unblock work, leave an entry-level $comment noting the intended floor and the follow-up that restores it.

humans.name: adam
humans.affinityComment: Adam: remote-side bootstrap anchor — shem-only, no on-prem fallback. Per the 2026-05-27 placement directive, every non-family persona is pinned to remote (shem); Pending if shem is down is intentional fail-loud behavior. Adam's pod is rendered from adam-firstman.yaml (manifest, not template), which is already hard-pinned to node-type=remote — the nodeTypes value here is informational and not consumed for adam.
humans.$genesisPeerComment: Adam + Matthew form the genesis pair WHEN shem is available: each ingests content directly during seeding so the payload settles across two peers in parallel. Adam is remote-only (nodeTypes:['remote'], pinned to shem), so the seeder now HOLDS adam from the genesis set whenever the remote pool is down (ELOHIM_REMOTE_COMPUTE_STATUS=unavailable / cluster-state.yaml shem:false) and matthew (household) carries genesis alone. The gate is at CONSUMPTION (genesis/Jenkinsfile runContentSeedStage substrate-aware filter), so this static genesisPeer:true stays correct-when-shem-is-up and no longer drifts as shem comes and goes (feedback_shem_down_peers_are_held).
humans.$resumedComment: shem returned 2026-05-18 (decommissioned 2026-05-04 PSU failure; 40 GiB openebs-hostpath PVC was unrecoverable). Re-enabling on fresh PVC — original seeded chain is lost, so seed will bootstrap a new agent key. Genesis pair (adam+matthew) reactivates without pipeline edit; pipeline tolerates 1..N genesis peers.

Matthew (household) is the always-on genesis peer; the seeder holds adam (remote-only) when shem is down, so matthew-carries-genesis-alone is the steady state while remote compute is unavailable. humans.$comment2: SECOND BUMP (2026-06-04): OOMKilled again AT the 3Gi limit — Prometheus-verified (kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason=OOMKilled, pod uid 077c96c0, restart ~21:30Z; prior pod uid 60f36d5d restarted ~17:20Z; pod replaced ~20:05Z by the edge deploy). $recycledLaptopFloor.$comment: 2026-06-10: floor raised from 512Mi/1536Mi to 768Mi/3Gi. OOM evidence (constraint=CONSTRAINT_MEMCG, anon-rss ~1488MiB) confirms Holochain conductor cold-start RSS exceeds 1536Mi reliably — 1536Mi is no longer a valid floor for any shem-placed peer running a full conductor. 3Gi is the validated minimum (james stable at ~2.1Gi RSS; jessica stable at ~1.4Gi on a quieter load profile). Restoration path: profile conductor cold-start with /proc/meminfo under shem-stable conditions; if baseline RSS drops sustainably below 1Gi (e.g. after a conductor memory footprint improvement), step the floor down in 512Mi increments with observed-RSS evidence.

humans.$memoryBumpComment2: 2026-06-13: edgenodeMemoryLimit 3Gi → 8Gi (request 768Mi → 2Gi), mirroring the operator's live `kubectl set resources` after james OOM-crashlooped at 3Gi (~9-min cycle, exit 137; james carries the LARGEST corpus, 3654 docs). This is the Nth bump in the chain — ROOT CAUSE now documented: at target_arc_factor=1 the embedded conductor holds a full authority arc, so its DHT working set is proportional to the whole corpus; a lean device-chromebook-edu archetype fundamentally cannot hold james's full arc and no RAM bump reconciles that. 8Gi is a STOPGAP to stop the re-OOM on the next Jenkins re-apply, NOT a chromebook floor. DURABLE FIX = arc-shrink (target_arc_factor < 1 → bounded shard per node) — see genesis/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-13-conductor-authority-arc-memory-scaling.md (answers jessica's 2026-06-04 'profile elohim-node for a leak' breadcrumb). Restoration: when the arc-factor policy lands, step back toward $chromebookFloor with observed-RSS evidence. NB jessica (4Gi) is climbing too and is the next to OOM under load — same fix, do not chase it with more RAM.
humans.$arcFactorComment: 2026-06-16: target_arc_factor 1->0 (leecher). james carries the LARGEST corpus (3654 docs) at a full authority arc, so its conductor working set is proportional to the whole corpus and OOM-cycles at its 8Gi limit (live 5.82GB and climbing) on the shared ethosengine box next to matthew — exactly the durable fix this entry's $memoryBumpComment2 named ('DURABLE FIX = arc-shrink'). Validated lever: jessica's identical flip boots HolochainP2pConfig{target_arc_factor:0} and runs at 1.34GB leecher. james is NOT a genesis peer (only adam+matthew are, genesisPeer:true), so no partition risk: matthew+adam+the shem nodes stay full-arc holders of the whole keyspace (12 full holders remain; coverage safe — the deploy sed path bypasses coverage_admits so this is a hand-verified call). Freeing ~5GB on ethosengine relieves matthew's doorway watchdog co-location park (RCA theory 3). Household durability is unaffected (Plane B storage-plane RS shards on disk, not Plane A authority arc). Revert to 1 to undo. See genesis/docs/content/elohim-protocol/history/2026-06-15-matthew-edge-resiliency-rca-fanout-synthesis.md + genesis/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-13-conductor-authority-arc-memory-scaling.md.

humans.$comment: Introduced 2026-05-18 alongside shem-return reshuffle. Gertrude formalizes the 'grandma standard' archetype that has shaped the resilience epic — the non-technical user who must be served well (memory: project_recovery_grandma_standard, project_subsume_g_f_a_via_it_just_works). She is the reciprocal-recovery counterparty for the Dowell household: gertrude ↔ matthew/jessica/james hold each other's Shamir-split shares for social-derived recovery (memory: project_socially_derived_security, project_graduated_recovery_authority). Dowell-side hub is matthew's device-family-node-base (on-prem family hub); gertrude is modeled here as her always-on hub-class device (device-home-nuc) — she also has a laptop in real life, but the per-human-multi-device topology isn't modeled in deployments yet; the hub holds the Shamir share so the backup relationship is exercisable from this one entry. We have not yet hit high-availability or fully-realized backup, but this single reciprocal relationship is enough to test the full recovery/sharding/login story surface. Structural schema for these stewardship agreements deferred — captured first in canonical stories under genesis/data/stories/ until the field shape crystallizes; humans.schema.json is protocol-law and any extension wants story-first justification.

Susan lives in Seattle, WA with her husband Caleb and three young children (not yet on the protocol) — see human-caleb-spouse deployment record. Susan-and-Caleb form the Pacific NW leg of a tri-region reciprocal backup chain: Dowell-household (matthew/jessica/james, San Antonio TX) ↔ Susan's household (susan/caleb, Seattle WA) ↔ Gertrude's household (gertrude, San Antonio TX), with Daniel's household (Jessica's brother, Tulsa OK) added as a fifth replicator giving the chain a third independent region. Multi-region geographic separation means no single natural disaster, ISP outage, or regional power failure can take down both halves of any reciprocal pair simultaneously — load-bearing for the 'high-availability' tier of the resilience epic (genesis/docs/content/elohim-protocol/resilience/README.md:146). Typical-steward floor mirrors jessica's $recycledLaptopFloor (device-recycled-laptop). Remote placement (remote/performance) lands Susan on shem when available so she is physically distant from the Dowell on-prem hub — geographic resilience reflected in K8s placement.

Remote/performance placement on shem gives geographic-storyline separation from the Dowell on-prem cluster.
